<Heading
  as={"h1"}

  children={"Execute Resource Command"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/actions/{command}"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Executes the command declared in the type definition of the resource. The request body only allows `id` and `input`: `id` must be a non-empty string, `input` must be an object, and extra fields will be rejected.
The specific input, output, and available commands are based on the runtime definition returned by GET /resource-types/\{type\}.
Common protocol resource commands:
  - For `create`, the `id` is `protocol:{protocolId}`; do not provide parentId when creating a network; parentId is required for creating devices/points.
  - For `discover`, the `id` is `protocol:{protocolId}`.
  - For `import`, the `id` is the discovery job resource ID.
  - For `delete`, the `id` is the resource ID to be deleted, and `input` must be an empty object.

For `import`: The `ownerId` to import must point to the same running instance as the owner recorded by the server during discovery; other owners of the same protocol/type will still be rejected. Protocol, ownerKind, and targetKind must also match, and candidates must belong to the job. Old tasks missing complete server context cannot use client parameters for supplementation, and all checks are completed before batch creation. If inconsistent, returns PROTOCOL_CONFIG_INVALID (2103, HTTP 422); if the task with a located protocol lacks owner/target context, returns DISCOVERY_JOB_NOT_FOUND (2111, HTTP 400); if the task or protocol association cannot be located, returns RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND (2121, HTTP 404), and no objects are created.

For `sequence` resources:
  - For `create`, the `id` is `sequence`. `input` allows `name`, `data`, `icon`, and `deviceId`, of which `name`, `data`, and `deviceId` are required.
  - `deviceId` specifies the device the scene is created for. `create` only accepts `data.type=commands` and does not accept `unavailable`.
